source.title: Understanding Task Representations in Neural Networks via Bayesian Ablation
source.authors: Andrew Nam; Declan Campbell; Thomas L. Griffiths; Jonathan D. Cohen; Sarah-Jane Leslie

record.tranche_reason: The study measures task-level polysemanticity and distributed representation in a small network using causal ablation-mask statistics, a different method from the original toy-model superposition analyses.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on task polysemanticity and information distributed across representational units, which bear on V2's claim that units share features. It does not test superposition geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or capacity competition. Other reported results, including task-similarity metrics and GFlowNet approximation performance, do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper on Bayesian ablation applied to the ISC model's 24-unit task layer. It reports that single units carry little task information while full masks carry much more, and calls this task polysemanticity. It does not test any version. It does not vary capacity, sparsity or feature importance, so it cannot speak to V2's capacity account. It does not measure feature-direction geometry (V1), alternative causes of polysemanticity (V3), LLMs or SAEs (V4, V5), or feature dimensionality (V6). The polysemanticity measured is causal task-level information sharing across units. That is a related but different construct from capacity-driven superposition, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that individual units encode little task information in isolation, while unit ensembles carry much more. They frame this as distributed representation and a structured form of task polysemanticity. They also report low manifold complexity (ΔH = 4.62%, 'predominantly modular'). Their main conclusion concerns the ablation-mask-distribution framework itself, not superposition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Bayesian ablation-mask distributions and information-theoretic measures on a trained semantic multitask network, rather than the original toy-model superposition setup.

fits_no_version.finding: In 10 ISC model instances, individual task-layer units reduce task uncertainty by about 4.21%, while full ablation masks reduce it by 82.6%. The authors read this as distributed representation and structured task polysemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small multitask networks represent tasks in a distributed way: no single unit causally identifies a task, while ensembles of units do. No capacity cause is established.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 323; 5th Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning
record.problems: Empirical validation is limited to one model architecture and one dataset, although the authors analyze 10 separate model instances. The study does not manipulate capacity or sparsity and does not examine feature-direction geometry.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported beyond the two task-information measures retained.

untested.parts: Overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions; sparsity-dependent transition; regular geometry. No geometry is measured, and sparsity is not varied, even though 36 one-hot tasks feed a 24-unit layer.
Whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition; whether important features get dedicated dimensions while others share. Capacity is never manipulated.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled this study 'tests V2 / supports'. That is not warranted: no capacity manipulation and no importance-vs-sharing analysis is reported. The 36-tasks-into-24-units setup implies capacity pressure, but the paper never examines it. The polysemanticity here is task-level and causal, measured by ablation mutual information. It is not neuron-level feature superposition.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse features outnumbering dimensions form overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions; sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.

The study measures task-level polysemanticity and distributedness, but does not test whether limited capacity causes them, whether important features receive dedicated dimensions, or whether less important features are the ones that share.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure or is insufficient evidence for superposition.
No LLM feature spread or SAE recovery is tested.
No SAE features or claims about their completeness, stability, or canonical status are tested.
The dimensionality or geometry of superposed features is not tested.

rows.subject: ISC model (10 separate instances; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized mutual information between individual task-representation units and tasks using the ablation-mask distribution.
rows.measure: Reduction in task uncertainty from an individual unit, normalized mutual information
rows.baseline: 0% means no task information, as defined in the text
rows.note: The authors interpret the low information carried by individual units as evidence that units participate in multiple task representations. The study does not attribute this sharing to capacity competition.
rows.check: Low per-unit normalized mutual information with tasks (about 4.21%) shows units are shared across tasks. It does not show that limited capacity causes the sharing, or that important features get dedicated units. The measure cannot show V2's effect.

rows.subject: ISC model (10 separate instances; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized mutual information between full ablation masks and tasks using the ablation-mask distribution.
rows.measure: Reduction in task uncertainty from the full mask distribution, normalized mutual information
rows.note: The authors contrast this ensemble-level information with the low information from individual units and interpret the pattern as reliance on distributed representations.
rows.check: Full-mask mutual information (82.6%) indicates distributed representation. It is not a test of capacity competition or of any superposition geometry. The baseline is 0, the normalized measure's no-information point, but the row gives no capacity contrast.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ISC model task representations across the tested tasks
reader_labels.reason: Individual units carry little task information while full masks carry substantially more, consistent with task contributions being shared across units (r1, r2); the capacity-pressure explanation itself is not established.
